title: The axioms of probability do not say what probability means
body: The Stanford Encyclopedia entry "Interpretations of Probability" separates a formal theory from its readings. Kolmogorov's axiomatization is the usual formal theory: a function on events obeying stated rules. The entry then distinguishes interpretations that say what that function is about. Frequency interpretations tie probability to long-run relative frequency. Subjective interpretations tie it to degrees of belief, updated as evidence comes in. Propensity interpretations tie it to a physical tendency of a setup. Best-system interpretations tie it to the role of probability in a simple strong summary of the world. The axioms constrain all of these. They do not choose among them. A calculation can be correct under the axioms and still be attached to a disputed meaning. This card does not pick an interpretation.
said_by: The survey of interpretations in the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

contested_views.position: Probability is a degree of belief.
Probability is a physical propensity of a chance setup.
